raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`Glm47MoeDetector` (`glm47`) and its `IQuestQ1Detector` subclass (`iquest_q1`) scan model output with patterns that go quadratic on unpaired tags:

1. **Tool-call blocks:** `detect_and_parse` runs `re.finditer` / `re.findall` with `<tool_call>.*?</tool_call>`, which rescans to the end of the text from every opening tag when the closing tag never arrives.
2. **Arguments:** `<arg_key>(.*?)</arg_key>(?:\\n|\s)*<arg_value>(.*?)</arg_value>`. Every `<arg_key>` whose pair never completes rescans the rest of the call. The same `findall` also runs in `_finalize_tool_call` (streaming), and `IQuestQ1Detector` runs it through `findall` + `sub`.

| Input | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 96 KB of `<tool_call> `, non-stream | 18.8 s | < 1 ms |
| 160 KB call of repeated `<arg_key>a</arg_key>`, non-stream | 24.9 s | 57 ms |
| same, the **single streaming chunk** that closes the call | 26.8 s | 24 ms |

Tool-call parsing runs synchronously on the tokenizer manager's event loop, so one such response stalls every in-flight request. Found with an Atheris fuzzing harness that records per-input parse time.

## Modifications

- `_iter_tool_call_spans`: a linear `str.find` scan returning the same spans `finditer` did. The unused `func_call_regex` is removed.
- `iter_arg_pair_matches`: a linear scanner yielding the same `(start, end, key, value)` matches as `finditer` on the argument regex. It first records each `</arg_key>` that is followed by a value opener; each key then ends at the first such tag after it, which is exactly where the lazy regex stops. `find_arg_pairs` replaces every `func_arg_regex.findall`, and `IQuestQ1Detector` derives its `findall` / `sub` results from the same matches.
- Regression test in `TestGlm47MoeDetector` (fails on `main`, passes here).

## Accuracy Tests

- Scanner vs `re.finditer` on the argument regex: identical on 600k random and mutated strings (458k matches).
- Differential test of `main` vs patched detectors (`glm47` and `iquest_q1`), comparing `detect_and_parse` and every streaming result under random re-chunking: **0 mismatches** over 40k random plus 60k mutated well-formed inputs.
- `test/registered/unit/function_call/`: 630 passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

See the table above.

Related: #42573, #42574 (same issue class in the dots and GLM-4.5 / Ling3 parsers).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (N/A)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

@@ -298,6 +298,43 @@ def parse_arguments(
         return json_value, False
 
 
+_ARG_VALUE_HEAD_REGEX = re.compile(r"(?:\\n|\s)*<arg_value>")
+
+
+# Yields (start, end, key, value) exactly as re.finditer would for
+# `<arg_key>(.*?)</arg_key>(?:\\n|\s)*<arg_value>(.*?)</arg_value>` (DOTALL).
+# Linear on purpose: that regex rescans to the end from every unpaired `<arg_key>`.
+def iter_arg_pair_matches(text: str):
+    # A key ends at the first `</arg_key>` that is followed by a value opener.
+    heads = []
+    close = text.find("</arg_key>")
+    while close != -1:
+        head = _ARG_VALUE_HEAD_REGEX.match(text, close + len("</arg_key>"))
+        if head is not None:
+            heads.append((close, head.end()))
+        close = text.find("</arg_key>", close + 1)
+
+    head_idx = 0
+    start = text.find("<arg_key>")
+    while start != -1:
+        key_start = start + len("<arg_key>")
+        while head_idx < len(heads) and heads[head_idx][0] < key_start:
+            head_idx += 1
+        if head_idx == len(heads):
+            return
+        key_end, value_start = heads[head_idx]
+        value_end = text.find("</arg_value>", value_start)
+        if value_end == -1:
+            return
+        end = value_end + len("</arg_value>")
+        yield start, end, text[key_start:key_end], text[value_start:value_end]
+        start = text.find("<arg_key>", end)
+
+
+def find_arg_pairs(text: str) -> List[Tuple[str, str]]:
+    return [(key, value) for _, _, key, value in iter_arg_pair_matches(text)]
+
